subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Placenta Praevia: Painless Bleeding and Double Setup

steps.tx: Implantation of the placenta over or near the internal os is **placenta praevia**. It causes painless, causeless, recurrent bright red bleeding in late pregnancy. Digital vaginal examination is forbidden until praevia is excluded by scan. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Placenta praevia implants over the os and causes painless recurrent bright bleeding.

steps.tx: Bleeding without pain, contractions or evident cause characterises **painless bleeding** of praevia. The uterus stays soft and the fetal heart usually remains normal. This contrasts sharply with the painful bleeding of abruption. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: Painless bleeding with a soft uterus characterises praevia against painful abruption.

steps.tx: Slowing of the fetal heart after a bleed as the head compresses the placenta is the **Stallworthy sign**. It historically suggested posterior placenta praevia before ultrasound. Today transvaginal scanning gives the diagnosis safely and precisely. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: The Stallworthy sign historically suggested posterior praevia before ultrasound diagnosis.

steps.tx: Examination in theatre with full caesarean readiness, historically used to feel the placenta, is the **double setup examination**. Ultrasound has made it nearly obsolete. It survives only where imaging is unavailable and delivery is imminent anyway. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: Double setup examination in theatre is now nearly obsolete thanks to ultrasound.

steps.tx: Transvaginal ultrasound measures the distance from placental edge to os as the **edge to os distance**. Under two centimetres near term usually means caesarean delivery. Many low placentas migrate upward as the lower segment develops. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Edge to os distance under two centimetres near term usually means caesarean delivery.

steps.tx: Most low lying placentas at twenty weeks move clear by term through apparent **placental migration**. The lower segment stretching carries the edge away from the os. A follow up scan at thirty two to thirty six weeks decides the birth plan. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Placental migration clears most low placentas by term as the lower segment stretches.

steps.tx: Major praevia covering the os needs planned caesarean at thirty six to thirty seven weeks, termed **planned delivery timing**. Unstable bleeding at any gestation forces immediate delivery. Blood is cross matched and consent includes possible hysterectomy. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Major praevia delivers by planned caesarean at thirty six to thirty seven weeks.

steps.tx: Praevia over a previous caesarean scar strongly predicts abnormally adherent placenta, the **praevia accreta link**. This combination produces the most dangerous haemorrhage in modern obstetrics. Antenatal diagnosis and planned surgery in specialist centres save lives. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Praevia over a caesarean scar predicts accreta and needs specialist planned surgery.

steps.tx: Speculum examination is safe and useful in antepartum haemorrhage to exclude local causes, termed **speculum assessment**. It reveals cervical lesions, polyps and the amount of bleeding. Only digital examination waits for scan exclusion of praevia. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Speculum assessment is safe in antepartum bleeding while digital examination waits for scanning.
